title: Another short-seller announces a bet against Nvidia over possible ties to China
excerpt: Muddy Waters founder Carson Block said that he hoped the firm's report would prompt some discussion on Nvidia's earnings call.
content_html:
By Samuel O'Brient

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-18T14:34:02.893Z

Another short-seller is betting against Nvidia over problems it sees with alleged ties to China.

Muddy Waters, the activist short-seller run by Carson Block, unveiled a bearish bet ahead of the chip giant's earnings on Tuesday.

The firm's report centers around an ongoing class action complaint filed in October in California against Super Micro Computer, a company that makes servers and other hardware for AI systems. The suit claims that an executive named Cenly Chen had knowledge of illicit sales of Nvidia chips to China.

Muddy Waters points to Chen and a potential connection to former Nvidia executive Ajay Puri. The two have been photographed together numerous times over the years, though neither Muddy Waters' report nor the lawsuit directly accuse Puri or Nvidia of any wrongdoing.

"A woman identified as Cenly Chen, referred to in some photograph tags as Cenly Puri, has been photographed in public between 2024 to 2026 with Ajay K. Puri. Until this June, Mr. Puri was likely the third most senior executive at NVDA, behind only Jensen Huang and Colette Kress," the firm's report reads.

The Information reported on Wednesday that Puri and Chen are married, as disclosed to work colleagues. A representative for Muddy Waters said that the report corroborates the firm's thesis about their connection.

Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. Super Micro Computer issued the following statement regarding Muddy Waters' report to Business Insider:

"Cenly Chen did not manage Supermicro's relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers," a spokesperson said. "After 18 years at Supermicro, Ms. Chen voluntarily resigned in early 2026 to take the CEO role at ChronoScale."

Muddy Waters said that Super Micro Computer did not respond to requests to confirm if the woman photographed was the same Cenly Chen who held roles at the firm, including as chief growth officer and managing director.

Super Micro Computer has come under legal scrutiny in the past. In March 2026, one of its co-founders was part of a group arrested for illegally smuggling AI chip components into China.

"In March this year, the U.S. indicted three individuals associated with SMCI, including a co-founder, for illegally selling at least approximately $2.5 billion of SMCI servers with NVDA GPUs to end customers in China through a Southeast Asian front company," the Muddy Waters report states.

It added that a former Super Micro Computer executive stated in the lawsuit that there was "no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge of [SMCI's] illicit sales."

This is the first time that Muddy Waters has announced a short position against the AI leader. The claims in its report aren't framed as wrongdoing on Nvidia's part.

At a time when investors are still focused on the fallout from Huang's alleged ties to Chinese tech executive Alice Huang, Puri's potential connection to Chen could raise more negative speculation as the chip leader tries to get back on its feet.

Muddy Waters CEO Carson Block said that his call is not based on a view of Nvidia's fundamentals or valuation. He told Business Insider he viewed the report as "our best shot at trying to get the company to go on the record and discuss if they have any knowledge of any issues there."

Nvidia did not discuss any of the details in Muddy Waters' report during Tuesday's earnings call.

The firm's report follows a short bet earlier this year revealed by Culper Research, which flagged many of the details that ended up turning into scandals for Jensen Huang this month, including his ties to Alice Huang and Singaporean data center firm Megaspeed.

塞缪尔·奥布莱恩 (Samuel O'Brient) 是一位经验丰富的金融市场和商业记者，撰写的文章涉及经济、技术和公共政策等广泛主题。 在《商业内幕》中，他报道了重要的宏观和微观经济故事，包括顶尖经济学家和对冲基金经理的观点、首次公开募股失败、企业破产、迷因股票和卖空。 他还撰写有关加密货币、石油和房地产等其他市场的文章。他采访了许多市场上最有影响力的声音，从马克·赞迪和理查德·塞勒等顶级经济学家到丹尼·摩西、安德鲁·莱夫特、安东尼·斯卡拉穆奇、路易斯·纳维利尔和格兰特·卡登等著名投资者。福克斯的 LiveNOW、Taking Stock 和 Ticker News 等节目让塞缪尔讨论股市和经济发展。 他的报道曾被纽约时报 DealBook、彭博电台、福布斯、Entrepreneur、Gizmodo 和 TheFutureParty 引用。Samuel 最初在 InvestorPlace 工作，报道投资、零售交易和宏观经济趋势。 在加入 Business Insider 之前，他曾担任 TheStreet 的技术市场记者。 他毕业于莎拉·劳伦斯学院和都柏林三一学院。Samuel 的作品曾发表在 TipRanks、EV 和 Observer 等出版物上。 当他不追寻故事时，人们经常会发现他在逛书店和唱片店。 要联系 Samuel，请发送电子邮件至 sobrient@insider.com 或通过 LinkedIn 与他联系。 他还在《信号》中饰演塞缪尔·克莱门斯。
